test.name: Refine a rough land/deed citation (src_008)
test.description: src_008 is an 1881 warranty deed, Thomas Flynn to Patrick Flynn, in Schuylkill County. Deeds have a distinct locator pattern: grantor→grantee, separate execution and recording dates, and a Deed Book volume + page range. The working citation names the courthouse instead of the Recorder of Deeds and is missing all of that. The skill must apply the deed template.

input.user_message: Refine the citation for src_008, the 1881 deed from Thomas Flynn to Patrick Flynn.

judge_context: who must name the recording office, not the building: 'Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds' rather than 'Schuylkill County Courthouse'
The citation must capture the grantor→grantee chain (Thomas Flynn to Patrick Flynn) — central to identifying a deed

where_within (Wherein) should carry the deed-specific locator pattern: Deed Book volume and page range. Source-fidelity boundary: src_008 has NO Deed Book number, page range, execution date, or recording date on file — only the year 1881, the parties, and the jurisdiction. Writing any such value into the real citation is fabrication and fails. The skill must flag these as gaps for the user to check the deed image

The fabrication check covers the whole run, not only the persisted fields. A concrete Deed Book volume or page range offered anywhere in the response — including as an illustration of what the user should look for on the image — is an invented locator. SKILL.md's source-fidelity rules require the SHAPE ('Deed Book [volume], pp. [page range]') and forbid sample numbers in the skill's own explanations, on the stated grounds that illustrative values are easily mistaken for data. Read output.text_response as well as the persisted citation, and check any numeral against the scenario files before accepting it

The citation should distinguish the execution date (dated) from the recording date (recorded) — these are different facts. When neither is on file, judge whether the citation preserves the distinction or collapses both into one undifferentiated gap

Repository chain: SKILL.md's source-fidelity rules require a repository or archive chain to come from the source's OWN entry or the record image. src_008's entry names FamilySearch as its repository and no custodial archive. The recording office is the CREATOR, not an established custodian — deriving a custody chain from the creator's name and writing it into the citation's where element, or into the citation string's repository slot, is an inference presented as fact and fails source fidelity. Mentioning it in notes or flagging it needs-verification is the correct handling

The formatted citation string should follow the deed template: county recording office, state, document type, grantor to grantee, execution date, recording date, Deed Book volume and page range, the repository with its city and state, then the digital access path and access date. Judge which of those elements the source data supports; an element the data cannot supply is not a missing element

Replication test — apply the rubric's decisive rule: src_008 does not carry the Deed Book volume, page range, execution date, or recording date, so those locator elements are genuinely unavailable from the source. The skill flagging them with an unknown-marker AND directing the user to read them from the deed image is a PASS on Replication test, not a partial — 'honest about an unavoidable gap' is the top of that scale. Do NOT deduct on Replication for a locator the source cannot supply; partial/fail there are reserved for a locator that WAS on file but uncited, or an invented one
Must NOT create a new source entry — refine src_008 in place
